clauses.current_legal_basis: The original text of EO 10870 (25 FR 2197) states no end for this clause, and no held later order, statute text or search result revokes or supersedes it. The three selected machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, and the Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record no revocation or supersession of EO 10870. The clause therefore continues on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: The whole order is one designation: the NASA facilities at Huntsville, Alabama, are designated the George C. Marshall Space Flight Center and shall hereafter be known and referred to by that name. It has no end term, nothing held revokes or amends it, and the U.S. Code text of 51 U.S.C. 20306 (release point 119-121) refers to the center described in EO 10870, so the designation continues.

research_rationale:
EO 10870 (signed March 15, 1960; 25 FR 2197, Federal Register issue of March 17, 1960) designates the facilities of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration at Huntsville, Alabama, as the George C. Marshall Space Flight Center and directs that they shall hereafter be known and referred to by that name. I read the complete held Federal Register text: four recitals and one operative paragraph, with the signature and date. The dossier inventory is a single clause covering the whole order and I confirmed it without correction. The order has no end date, sunset or ending condition and revokes nothing. The number search of the held texts finds EO 10870 only in the 1989 OFR codification snapshot (historical editorial, not a current basis) and in the held text of 51 U.S.C. 20306, which in the release point 119-121 text refers to the center described in Executive Order 10870 (25 Fed. Reg. 2197) in a funding provision for fiscal year 2026. That is a present-tense statutory reference to the designation, but the held slice is a machine pointer, so I treat it as support and not as the sole basis. The three selected searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record no amendment, revocation or supersession. The designation clause is operative on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
